headline_marked: [[Kansas town silences public comment]] on AI data center after death threats, moves to virtual meetings
headline: Kansas town silences public comment on AI data center after death threats, moves to virtual meetings
summary: Emporia, Kansas, moves city council meetings online and cancels public comment after receiving death threats related to a proposed gigawatt AI data center. This follows a teacher's arrest for clapping at a previous hearing.
details: The Emporia, Kansas city council has moved its meetings online and canceled public comment periods for upcoming sessions. This decision comes after council members reportedly received death threats concerning a proposed gigawatt AI data center. The move follows a prior incident where a physics teacher was arrested for clapping in support of data center opposition.

While the city cited public safety as the reason for virtual meetings, it directed citizens to email and phone for concerns, eliminating direct public input. This led to some residents protesting outside the municipal auditorium, expressing frustration over the lack of open dialogue.

One citizen, previously arrested, questioned the credibility and origin of the threats, suggesting they might not be local. They acknowledged the need for safety but criticized the complete removal of public comment, stating they don't understand why it was necessary.

The council also unanimously voted to send a petition for a data center ban to judicial review, claiming that outright approval or denial could lead to lawsuits. This cautious approach may be influenced by warnings in other states about the legal challenges of imposing such bans.
